title: Remove, Dedupe, Intersect
hints:
You cannot erase inside a range-for: it has no iterator to hand to `erase`, and even if it did, erasing invalidates the iterator the loop is holding. Use the erase-remove idiom instead: `std::remove` shifts the keepers to the front and returns the new logical end; `erase` chops the tail.

```cpp
v.erase(std::remove(v.begin(), v.end(), x), v.end());
```
